steps.message: The fix involves modifying `Text.wrap` in `rich/text.py` to handle `soft_wrap` (where `no_wrap=True` and `overflow="ignore"`) by wrapping the text and joining the resulting segments into a single `Text` object. This ensures that background styles are repeated at the wrap points, allowing them to persist across terminal-initiated soft wraps without inserting hard newline characters.

The bug was that background styles were not preserved when `soft_wrap=True` was used in `console.print`, because `rich` would send the entire text as a single line, and some terminals do not continue background styles across soft wraps. The fix modifies `Text.wrap` so that when `soft_wrap` is active (indicated by `no_wrap=True` and `overflow="ignore"`), the text is still wrapped to calculate wrap points, and the styles are explicitly repeated at those points within a single `Text` object. This ensures background styles persist across terminal wraps without inserting actual newline characters.
